web/vendor/avatar/jim.vrm

Seed-san, by VirtualCast, Inc.

Source:    https://github.com/vrm-c/vrm-specification
Path:      samples/Seed-san/vrm/Seed-san.vrm
License:   VRM Public License 1.0, https://vrm.dev/licenses/1.0/
Copyright: VirtualCast, Inc.
SHA-256:   624d0d554bc205bbdc33e22a68a2c3c20edebb3e573011ead8878a65e5329b23
Bytes:     10917800

CodeTrial renders this model as its interviewer, "Jim". The character is
VirtualCast's, not CodeTrial's, and is used under the grant below.

The grant travels inside the file. VRM Public License 1.0 takes its terms from
the VRMC_vrm.meta block of the model itself rather than from any web page, so
what follows is that block, read verbatim out of the bytes committed here:

  "name":              "Seed-san"
  "authors":           ["VirtualCast, Inc."]
  "copyrightInformation": "VirtualCast, Inc."
  "licenseUrl":        "https://vrm.dev/licenses/1.0/"
  "avatarPermission":  "everyone"
  "commercialUsage":   "corporation"
  "modification":      "allowModificationRedistribution"
  "allowRedistribution": true
  "creditNotation":    "required"

CREDIT IS REQUIRED. "creditNotation": "required" obliges any use of this model
to name its author. CodeTrial satisfies that by crediting VirtualCast, Inc. in
the lobby footer of web/index.html, in README.md, in NOTICE, and here. It sat
beneath the avatar during the interview and was moved out because it crowded
the workspace. Moving it is fine; dropping it is not, and
tests/browser/avatar.test.js asserts a visible credit still exists in the UI.

Reproduce this file:

  curl -L -o jim.vrm \
    https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vrm-c/vrm-specification/master/samples/Seed-san/vrm/Seed-san.vrm
  shasum -a 256 jim.vrm

Re-read the embedded grant at any time:

  node -e 'const b=require("fs").readFileSync("jim.vrm");
    const j=JSON.parse(b.slice(20,20+b.readUInt32LE(12)).toString("utf8"));
    console.log(JSON.stringify(j.extensions.VRMC_vrm.meta,null,2))'
